resumen: The same movement as the barbell Romanian deadlift, with a dumbbell in each hand: the hips go back, the knees barely bend and the dumbbells travel down in front of the legs.
ejecucion: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs and your feet hip-width apart.
Push your hips back with your knees almost fixed and let the dumbbells travel down close to your legs.
Go down while your back stays flat; when it starts to round, that is the end of your range.
Come back up by driving your hips forward until you are standing, without leaning back.
matices: With dumbbells the load is usually lighter than with a barbell, which makes the movement easier to learn; on the other hand, each hand moves on its own and they have to be coordinated. Activation studies have mostly used a barbell: in the barbell Romanian deadlift, the cited review finds more hamstring than erector activity.
